messages:
maria: Heads-up — we should add a lint that flags when route header overrides can shadow or bypass quota annotations. Hit a customer bug where a per-team quota stopped applying because a header set on the route changed routing logic.

alex: Can you paste the snippet that caused it?

maria: Yeah, simplified form: 
```yaml
routes:
  - match: /api/*
    headers:
      set:
        X-User-Tier: enterprise
    quotas:
      requests_per_minute: 1000
```
In this case the console had a higher-level quota declaration intended for /api/* but an upstream author used header set to route to an enterprise variant that accidentally bypassed quota enforcement (our runtime matches header-based overrides before quota resolution).

jamal: Hmm. Two risks: (1) false positives if header sets are innocuous, (2) config authors sometimes intentionally move quotas elsewhere. We need a heuristic, not a hard block.

alex: Agreed. Proposal: lint with two severities — "info" when a header override exists without an explicit quota on the same route, "warn" if the override alters matching headers that affect quota keys (Authorization, X-Customer-ID, X-Billing-Tier).

maria: That feels reasonable. Also suggest we detect if the header value widens scope, e.g., set X-Tier: "*" or set a static value that flips to a higher tier. We could conservative-check for string literals vs templated values.

leo: Would be nice if the console shows an inline hint: small badge next to the header block "lint: quota-shadow" with hover text + link to runbook. Clicking opens an example diff to fix. UX should avoid modal spam. :thumbsup:

jamal: Implementation plan:
- Add rule in config-lint: header-quota-shadowing.
- Rule checks: presence of header set/append/remove; if header in (Authorization, X-Customer-ID, X-Billing-Tier, X-User-Tier) then severity=warn.
- If route has quotas defined explicitly -> lower severity.
- Add unit tests with examples (positive/negative).

alex: Telemetry idea: instrument lint hits by route id + observed runtime delta in quota counters. If we see routes flagged by lint but no runtime delta for 30d, lower severity automatically. This avoids long tail noise.

maria: Nice. Also add a quick pre-commit fixer that suggests adding explicit quotas or moving header logic into a matching predicate instead of set. Example autofix: convert header set -> matcher: 
```yaml
# before
headers:
  set:
    X-User-Tier: enterprise
# after
match_headers:
  X-User-Tier: enterprise
```

jamal: CI note: ci-bot can run lint on PRs and post annotation. I'll add a test harness.

ci-bot: @jamal created issue config-lint#412 with reproducer and initial test cases.

alex: One more question — do we want this rule only in the Console preflight flow, or also in the CLI and API?

leo: All of the above. Preflight in Console should show richer hints + autofix UI; CLI should output machine-friendly JSON for CI; API should return the same lint codes for programmatic flows.

maria: OK action items:
- jamal: PR adding lint rule + tests (ETA 3d)
- alex: telemetry event spec + list of observed counters to track (ETA 1 week)
- leo: console hint copy + small UX sketch (ETA 2d)
- ci-bot: annotate incoming PRs once lint lands

jamal: I'll open the PR today and add the unit tests and a few negative examples.

alex: Thanks — this should prevent another surprise customer escalation.

leo: :rocket:

maria: Thanks all, will add a short note in the routing authoring runbook after we merge.
